verdict.rationale: Qdrant's docs say users can 'use cloud-hosted embedding models directly with Qdrant', a first-party claim of in-database embedding via configured providers. The evidence is a single overview line, though. One hands-on community report says embeddings had to be generated client-side; that comment likely predates the feature and may refer to self-hosted use, so it lowers confidence rather than establishing a dispute. Missing for 10: documentation that embeddings are generated at both ingest and query time, the list of supported or configurable model providers, any built-in local models, whether self-hosted deployments are covered, and independent hands-on confirmation.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can have the database generate embeddings at ingest and query time using built-in or configured model providers, instead of running a separate embedding pipeline

citations.quote: Use cloud-hosted embedding models directly with Qdrant.
